taxonomic_note: Accepted at species rank as Prunus rivularis Scheele. The reviewed var. pubescens concept is treated as a heterotypic synonym for county-evidence mapping; do not automatically merge all Prunus murrayana records.
look_here_first: Start with growth form and the short flowering shoots: creek plum is a clonal, thicket-forming shrub with alternate simple serrate leaves, small white flower clusters on short shoots, and rounded single-stoned plum fruits. Check leaf-margin glands when present, but do not require them on older leaves because they can be shed.

project_inclusion.range_basis: B159 review: Kerr supported by a published herbarium voucher; Concho and Edwards supported under the reviewed P. rivularis var. pubescens synonym in expert Texas county-flora literature.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Williamson is outside the project target zone. The known Hays occurrence used in earlier discussion is introduced and is not counted as native-range evidence.

best_field_traits: clonal thicket-forming shrub with spreading shallow roots
alternate simple leaves with toothed margins
leaf-margin glands may be present but can be shed as leaves mature
small white flower clusters borne on short shoots
rounded drupe with a single hard stone
reviewed UT local treatment describes shoots as not spinescent; do not teach universal thorniness
morphology_keys.leaves: Alternate, simple and serrate; glands may occur near the margin but absence on mature leaves is not decisive.
morphology_keys.flower: Small white Prunus flowers clustered on short shoots; confirm the plum/cherry floral plan rather than relying on color.
morphology_keys.fruit: Rounded plum-like drupe containing one stone.
morphology_keys.habit: Usually a clonal thicket-forming shrub rather than the small-tree habit typical of Mexican plum.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Use clonal shrub habit, short-shoot flower arrangement, leaf characters and mature drupe together. Mexican plum is typically a small tree; black cherry develops raceme-type flower/fruit clusters. Do not separate creek plum from Chickasaw plum by range alone.
